# Schema Validator

> Free, client-only JSON Schema validator. Validates JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, and CSV data against
> a JSON Schema (draft-07, 2019-09, 2020-12) entirely in the browser — no server, no sign-up,
> no data ever leaves the device.

Core capability: paste or upload a JSON Schema and a data file in any supported format; get
back structured validation errors with line numbers, plain-English explanations, and one-click
fixes. Also supports OpenAPI/Swagger schema import, batch validation of an array of records,
schema inference from sample data, sample data generation, and format conversion between the
five supported data formats.

## Pages

- [Schema Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/): the main app — validate JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, or CSV against a JSON Schema.
- [JSON Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/json-validator/): JSON syntax checking and schema validation.
- [YAML Schema Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/yaml-validator/): validating YAML specifically.
- [OpenAPI Schema Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/openapi-validator/): importing an OpenAPI/Swagger spec and validating against one of its component schemas.
- [CSV Schema Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/csv-validator/): batch-validating every row of a CSV file.
- [TOML Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/toml-validator/): validating TOML config files.
- [XML Validator](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/xml-validator/): validating XML against a JSON Schema instead of an XSD.
- [Blog](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/blog/): guides on JSON Schema drafts, OpenAPI vs. JSON Schema, and running schema checks in CI.
- [Privacy Policy](https://schema-validator-livid.vercel.app/#privacy): what's stored locally, AdSense cookie use, opt-out link.

## Notes for automated agents

- Everything runs client-side — there is no API endpoint to call for validation. To reproduce a
  check outside the browser, use the app's own "Copy as Node.js snippet" / "Copy as Python
  snippet" feature, which generates a self-contained ajv or jsonschema script.
- This is a single-page app with no server-rendered content beyond the landing pages listed
  above; the root URL's `#root` div is populated by JavaScript.
